Writing style can change with time and context, and it is not always stable enough to identify an author reliably. In a benchmark spanning 21 years, authorship verification worsened as the time between texts increased; genre shifts also affected verification, though some stylistic features remained stable across genres [2]. Scientific prose likewise showed changing trajectories across vocabulary, punctuation, readability, and syntax, with different features changing in different ways over time [4].

Text type matters: genre can influence stylistic features more strongly than whether text was written by a person or generated by an LLM [5]. Rewriting can also shift an individual’s style: LLM revisions tend to reduce personal markers and make narratives more polished and less situated [1], while privacy-focused rewriting can remove interactive and contextual cues [8].
